title: Hold a test probe on each passing pallet's pad for 2 s before the end line
instruction: Test both pallets as they pass: take the probe from its stand and hold its tip on each pallet's gold test pad for 2 seconds without a break, before the pallet reaches the red end line. The line keeps moving and won't stop for you.
context: On lines that run continuously, such as automotive final assembly, checks are made on the move: the operator walks with the part and holds a gauge or test probe on a test point long enough for a reading, then moves to the next part. A probe that slips off the point mid-reading gives no result and the part goes on untested. Done by: assembly-line inspectors and test operators.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table (110 x 130 cm). A conveyor line runs across the table from the right to the left, parallel to the line through the arm bases, its centre 32 cm in front of it: a black belt bed (14 cm wide, 124 cm long, 1.5 cm tall, ending 3 cm inside each table edge) with a low grey guide rail (5 mm wide, 1 cm tall) along each of its edges, and two grey aluminium pallets (12 x 12 x 3 cm) riding on its flat belt between the rails, square to it, their centres starting 20 cm and 50 cm to the right of the midpoint between the bases. Each pallet has a gold-plated test pad (3 x 3 cm, 4 mm thick) glued in the middle of its top, square to it; the pad is split into two interleaved combs (1 mm fingers, 0.3 mm gaps) wired to a coin cell and a green LED on the pallet's near side, so the LED lights only while something conductive (the brass tip) touches the pad. White tick marks (2 x 0.4 cm) are taped on the table beside the bed's far side every 10 cm, from 50 cm right of the midpoint to 30 cm left of it. Two strips of red tape (6 x 1.2 cm) mark the end line across the table on both sides of the bed, 40 cm to the left of the midpoint, 0.5 cm from the bed. The gripper's finger pads are covered with insulating tape. The test probe is one rigid part (no spring-loaded pin), 60 g: a black plastic square handle (2.6 x 2.6 x 10 cm) with a brass square tip (0.8 x 0.8 x 4 cm) fixed to the middle of its bottom face. It stands tip down in a stand of four wooden blocks (4.5 cm tall) glued to the table around a 1.6 x 1.6 cm square well: two 1 x 3.6 cm blocks on the near and far sides and two 1.6 x 1 cm blocks between them; the handle rests on the block tops with the tip hanging in the well, 0.5 cm above the table. The well's centre is 18 cm in front of the bases and 22 cm left of the midpoint. Nothing else is on the table. The line starts with the trial: the pallets speed up from rest to 4 cm/s in 0.5 s and run on at that speed, so their centres reach the end line 15.25 s and 22.75 s into the trial. The bed ends in a steel end stop (16 x 2 cm, 5 cm above the bed, rubber bumper face) bolted across its last 2 cm, 3 cm inside the table's left edge: the belt slips under pallets that reach it (or that anything holds back), so the first pallet waits against the bumper (centre 54 cm left of the midpoint) and the second against the first (centre 42 cm); no pallet leaves the line or the table.
scoring: The probe is on a pad at a control step (1/20 s) when its tip touches the pad throughout the step (sim: a PhysX contact sensor on the probe reports a probe-pad contact point with zero or negative separation at all 12 physics steps of the control step; real table: the pad's LED stays lit, lit by the held probe's tip), it is held by its handle (a gripper's grasp point, between the fingers, within 3 cm of the point on the handle's axis 3 cm below its top), it stands within 20 degrees of upright, the middle of its tip's end face is inside the pad's outline (seen from above) and no more than 0.2 mm above or 5 mm below the pad's top surface, the pad's centre is short of the end line, and its pallet is moving along the line at 3.5 cm/s or more (real table: 10 cm of tick marks in under 2.9 s). Hovering never counts; a dropped probe lying on the pad doesn't count. For each pallet, its longest unbroken time with the probe on its pad over the whole trial earns 1.0 for 2 s or more, 0.75 for 1.5 s, 0.5 for 1 s, 0.25 for any contact, 0 for none. The score is the mean of the two pallets' credits; 1.0 when both pallets were held for 2 s.
reset_notes: Stop the line, lift the pallets off the end stop and put them back at their starting positions, put the probe in its stand, and start the line with the trial.
fidelity: Pallets and pads follow their path exactly (a held-back real pallet stops as the belt slips; credit needs it moving), float 2 mm over the bed (a belt carries real ones), each pad 1 mm over its pallet (glued on), and stop dead at the end stop. The probe is rigid, as is the real one. Contact: PhysX contact reports (no gap) at every physics step in sim, the split pad's LED on a real table; the sim pad is one solid box.
